answer: Each identity enters through one inlet, locking a 60-credit bond and paying an epoch-count fee. The k-th admission pays 20+2(k-1) credits, so the 1,000th pays 2,018 and 1,000 fakes cost 1,019,000 in fees plus 60,000 in bonds. The plume ledger lists every admission, so auditors can recount, recompute fees, and slash underpaid bonds. Each identity keeps its thread of signed work; a lent thread breaks its chain and burns its bond. A shadow gateway fails, since only plume-recorded admissions earn rewards; an honest agent pays once and recovers its bond after three clean epochs.
